findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.validate_providers accepts provider-level dispatch_group: local, and hop_is_local inherits that label, but _build_provider_config copies only the model-level dispatch_group into ModelConfig.
findings.description: Provider-level local declarations do not activate the transport policy. An authenticated provider with dispatch_group: local, an HTTPS loopback endpoint, no insecure-endpoint opt-in, and models without individual dispatch_group labels passes validation but receives policy=None.
findings.failure_mode: Requests use environment proxies despite being classified as local. With HTTPS_PROXY configured, prompts and credentials can pass through the proxy; the urllib fallback also retains redirect following.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve effective locality consistently from both provider and model configuration, and activate TransportPolicy for every hop classified as local.

findings.cross_file_justification: The loader invokes validate_providers, but that function never invokes the separately defined validate_local_fallbacks check in endpoint_policy.py.
findings.description: The local fallback restriction is defined but disconnected from configuration loading. Under locality: local_voices, a valid local model whose fallback_chain names a hosted provider still passes the new validation gate.
findings.failure_mode: When the local hop fails, cheval can walk the configured fallback chain and send the prompt to the hosted provider despite the local_voices posture.
findings.suggested_fix: Invoke validate_local_fallbacks on the fully merged configuration after interpolation and alias resolution, before returning it from load_config.

findings.cross_file_justification: The head version of .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/config/endpoint_policy.py (_local_labels, hop_is_local, validate_local_fallbacks) treats a provider-block `dispatch_group: local` as a valid local label when the model entry is silent, and the loader admits it. cheval.py:_build_provider_config only reads `model_data.get("dispatch_group")`, and modelinv.py:hop_locality_of only reads the model entry, so the adapter and the MODELINV emitter disagree with the loader/planner about the same hop.
findings.description: ModelConfig.dispatch_group is populated solely from the model entry. A provider whose block carries `dispatch_group: local` (accepted by the loader's _local_label_refusal when the endpoint host passes the local rule, and counted as local by hop_is_local and the planner's fallback audit) produces ModelConfig.dispatch_group=None. OpenAIAdapter._transport_policy then returns None unless allow_insecure_endpoint is also set, so an https local hop runs without TransportPolicy: proxy environment variables are honoured, redirects are followed by urllib, and the path-prefix rule is not applied. modelinv.hop_locality_of likewise records `hop_locality: hosted` for a hop the planner dispatched as local under local_voices.
findings.failure_mode: Under `hounfour.locality: local_voices`, a provider labelled local at the block level (https endpoint on 127.0.0.1 / RFC1918, no opt-in) is dispatched through HTTPS_PROXY / follows a 3xx off-host, and the MODELINV audit row says hop_locality=hosted while the planner's locality gate counted it as local. The D-7.2 request-time guarantees and the D-8.0 audit field are both wrong for the same hop.
findings.suggested_fix: In _build_provider_config fall back to `prov.get("dispatch_group")` when the model entry has none (mirroring _local_labels / hop_is_local), and make modelinv.hop_locality_of delegate to endpoint_policy.hop_is_local(hounfour, provider, model_id) so there is one local-hop implementation. Add a test: provider-block label, model silent, https local endpoint, no opt-in -> TransportPolicy is non-None and MODELINV hop_locality == 'local'.

findings.description: destination_for returns `{host: cli-subprocess, scheme: cli}` whenever `not endpoint`, which is also the case when the provider name is not in hounfour.providers (prov == {}). The docstring and SDD reserve `cli` for `*-headless` types and `kind: cli` models. The second emit site in cmd_invoke feeds `_modelinv_state.get("final_model_id")` to hop_telemetry; if that value is a server-reported model id rather than the canonical `provider:model` hop (local servers such as Ollama return ids like `llama3.1:8b`, which split into provider `llama3.1`, model `8b`), an HTTP hop to a local server is recorded as a CLI subprocess destination.
findings.failure_mode: The MODELINV `destination` field, the audit evidence for where a prompt went, labels an unknown or mis-keyed HTTP hop as `cli-subprocess`, hiding a real network destination behind the one value that means 'no network'.
findings.suggested_fix: Return `{host: unknown, scheme: unknown}` when the provider block is missing or has no type/endpoint, and only return the cli marker for `*-headless` / `kind: cli`. At the emit site pass the canonical `_entry_target` of the answering hop rather than final_model_id, or assert the value contains a configured provider prefix before deriving destination.

findings.description: The policy text states an insecure endpoint 'is never resolved through DNS, so there is no rebinding', yet `localhost` is an admitted opt-in host and the adapters hand `http://localhost:<port>/...` to httpx/urllib, which resolve it via the system resolver (/etc/hosts, nsswitch, or a stub resolver). TransportPolicy.check_url compares the string host, not the resolved address, so nothing in the Python path pins localhost to loopback.
findings.failure_mode: On a host where `localhost` resolves to a non-loopback address (misconfigured /etc/hosts, container DNS), an opted-in plaintext http request carrying the prompt and any headers leaves the machine while every check reports a loopback-only posture. Documentation overstates the guarantee the code provides.
findings.suggested_fix: Either refuse `localhost` as an opt-in host and require an IP literal (127.0.0.1 / ::1), or resolve `localhost` once at request time and refuse unless every returned address is loopback; update the docstring to describe what is actually enforced.
